children: French engineering and technology group Technip Energies soared more than 8% on after a report said the company may be in line for a potential $10 billion contract with SpaceX.

Technip Energies is bidding to develop a rocket-fuel production facility at SpaceX's projected $100 billion base in Louisiana, French television BFM reported. The article said Elon Musk is anticipated to reveal the winning supplier.

The important thing about Technip's participation is the size of the potential payout. The corporation currently has close to a fifth of the world's liquefied natural gas liquefaction capacity and is adding to its assets in Louisiana, near property bought for the projected SpaceX plant.

Technip has reportedly offered to revise its under-construction Commonwealth LNG plant with an annual capacity of 9.5 million tons. But SpaceX's version would be different: it would use electrically powered turbines, not natural gas.

Reports say that SpaceX wants the fuel facilities built within 36 months. The wider Louisiana facility is slated to begin construction next year with the first Starship launch from the site scheduled for 2029.

One contract is not the only thing that is tempting to investors. A win would place Technip Energies into a vast infrastructure project meant to sustain thousands of future Starship launches. The near term significant catalyst will be if SpaceX truly awards Technip the estimated $10 billion.

title: Technip Energies Jumps 8% on a Possible $10 Billion SpaceX Deal
